mainTopic: Bringing a hand back into the same courtyard, removing bread from an oven on שבת, and why a hand needs no 4x4 place according to רבי עקיבא
overview: The amud opens by finishing the answer to two ברייתות that seemed to contradict each other. They concern a person who stuck his hand, full of fruit, out of his courtyard into the public domain on שבת. He may bring it back into the same courtyard but not into a different one, as רב נחמן ruled for רבא. The reason is that going back to the same courtyard defeats his plan, while going to a different courtyard completes it. The גמרא then discusses רב ביבי בר אביי's question about someone who stuck bread in an oven on שבת: may he take it out before it bakes? After testing several possible cases, and after רב ששת rejects רב שילא's answer, רב אשי concludes that the person acted on purpose. He may remove the bread so that he avoids an איסור סקילה. רב אחא בריה דרבא even teaches this as a plain ruling. Finally, the גמרא asks why the poor person in the משנה is liable when his hand is not a 4x4 place. רבה answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who holds קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to question whether רבה really treats that rule as obvious, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The prohibiting ברייתא refers to a different courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its answer: the ברייתא that forbids bringing the hand back is talking about bringing it into a different courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the ברייתא that forbids it is talking about bringing it to a different courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started on the previous amud. One ברייתא allows bringing the hand back, and one forbids it. The forbidding ברייתא is talking about bringing the hand into a different courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא said the permitting ברייתא is about bringing the hand back into the same courtyard. Now it gives the other half: the forbidding ברייתא is about a different courtyard. This removes the contradiction, because each ברייתא is talking about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, i.e., in this source; used to split two sources into two different cases
A different courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of an answer that began on the previous amud. The first half was 'כאן לאותה חצר', meaning 'here it means the same courtyard'.

phrases.english: Here, it refers to a different courtyard.
phrases.notes: Completes the answer 'כאן לאותה חצר, כאן לחצר אחרת'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a two-part answer to a contradiction between ברייתות that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to contradict each other about bringing the hand back.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing the hand back to the same courtyard is permitted. Bringing it to a different courtyard is forbidden.

steps.title: Source: רבא's question to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the split from a question רבא asked רב נחמן. Bringing the hand back to the same courtyard is permitted, and bringing it to a different courtyard is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבא asked רב נחמן: If a person's hand was full of fruit and he stuck it outside, may he bring it back into the same courtyard? He answered: It is permitted. What about bringing it to a different courtyard? He answered: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the split it just made already appears in a ruling of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asked about two cases, and רב נחמן ruled differently in each. Bringing the hand back to the same courtyard is permitted, and bringing it to a different courtyard is forbidden. This is exactly the line the גמרא drew between the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: As (so-and-so) asked of him
To bring it back
Permitted
Forbidden

phrases.english: As Rava asked Rav Naḥman:
If his hand was full of fruit
and he stuck it outside (into the public domain),
may he bring it back into the same courtyard?
He said to him: It is permitted.
What about bringing it to a different courtyard?
He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the split made in step 1 with an existing ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The split between bringing the hand back to the same courtyard and bringing it to a different courtyard.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's answers to רבא's question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: a person who stuck out his hand by mistake may bring it back to the same courtyard, but not to a different one.

steps.title: רבא asks why the two courtyards are different
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why there should be any difference, since both courtyards are private domains.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks why the two cases get different rulings. This question sets up רב נחמן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both courtyards are a רשות היחיד, a private domain. Carrying from the public domain into either one should be the same act. So רבא wants to know the reason for the different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference?

phrases.english: And what is the difference?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind רב נחמן's two different rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why the same courtyard and a different courtyard are treated differently.

steps.title: His plan was not done versus his plan was done
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן jokes that רבא would need to eat a כור of salt to figure it out. Then he explains: going back to the same courtyard undoes the person's plan, while going to a different courtyard completes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you eat a כור of salt over it, you will know. There, in the same courtyard, his plan was not carried out. Here, in a different courtyard, his plan was carried out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains the difference between the two cases. The key is whether the person's original plan ends up being achieved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person meant to move the fruit out of his courtyard. If he brings it back to the same courtyard, his plan fails, so allowing this is no reward for what he did. If he brings it to a different courtyard, the fruit really has been moved to a new place, so his plan succeeds. Because of that, the חכמים forbade it.

keyTerms.meaning: A כור (a large measure) of salt; an expression for long, hard thinking
Was carried out, was done
His plan or intention

steps.whatToRemember: Same courtyard is permitted because his plan was not carried out. A different courtyard is forbidden because his plan was carried out.

phrases.english: When you eat a kor of salt over it (you will understand).
phrases.notes: A joking remark meaning 'think it over long and hard'.

phrases.english: There (the same courtyard), his plan was not carried out.
Here (a different courtyard), his plan was carried out.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling depends on whether the person's original plan to move the fruit ends up being achieved.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Bringing the hand back to the same courtyard is allowed because it defeats his plan. Bringing it to a different courtyard is forbidden because it completes his plan.

steps.title: רב ביבי בר אביי's question about bread in the oven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now discusses רב ביבי בר אביי's question directly. If someone stuck bread in an oven on שבת, did the חכמים let him take it out before it bakes, so he avoids liability for a חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב ביבי בר אביי asked: If someone stuck bread onto the oven, did they permit him to remove it before he becomes liable for a חטאת, or did they not permit it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It now discusses in full a question that was mentioned earlier only in passing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing bread from the oven on שבת is forbidden by the חכמים. However, once the bread bakes, the person will have done a Torah-level מלאכה and will owe a חטאת. The question is whether the חכמים set aside their own rule so that he can avoid the Torah-level liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; returns to a statement that was quoted earlier in passing
Stuck (bread onto the oven wall)
To remove it (bread from the oven)
Liability to bring a sin-offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a basic question: may a person break a rabbinic rule in order to save himself from a Torah-level sin?

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav Beivai bar Abaye asked:
If someone stuck bread in the oven,
did they permit him to remove it
before he becomes liable for a sin-offering,
or did they not permit it?

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. בָּעֵי רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic: a question that was mentioned earlier only in passing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכמים allow removing the bread, which they normally forbid, so the person avoids a חטאת.

steps.title: רב אחא בר אביי asks what the case is
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אביי asks רבינא what situation רב ביבי's question could be talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אביי said to רבינא: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר אביי asks which situation the question is about. This sets up a list of possible cases that he will check one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before anyone can answer רב ביבי's question, the case has to be clear. Is the person acting by mistake or on purpose, and does he remember or not? רב אחא will test each possibility to see if it makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּיֵי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Abaye said to Ravina:
What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to clarify the case behind רב ביבי's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation רב ביבי's question is about.

steps.title: Ruling out someone who acted by mistake and never remembered
steps.stepSummary: If the person acted by mistake and still has not remembered, the question makes no sense. He does not know anything is wrong, so there is nobody to give permission to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he acted by mistake and has not remembered, to whom did they give permission?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא tests the first possible case and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who acted בשוגג and still does not realize it is שבת, or that this is forbidden, has no reason to ask about removing the bread. Permission only matters to someone who knows there is a problem. So the question cannot be about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggested case to test)
By mistake, unknowingly
He did not remember
To whom?

phrases.english: If you say it was by mistake
and he did not remember,
to whom did they give permission?
phrases.notes: He does not know there is a problem, so he would never ask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible case raised by the question in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the case of someone who acted by mistake and never remembered.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Someone who does not know he did anything wrong will not ask about removing the bread, so a permission would have no one to apply to.

steps.title: The case where he later remembers also fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a case where the person remembered before the bread baked. It rejects this, because a חטאת requires the whole act to be done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the case is where he then remembered before the bread baked? But would he even be liable for a חטאת then? We learned in a משנה: all who are liable for a חטאת are only liable if the act was by mistake at the beginning and by mistake at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible case for רב ביבי's question: the person remembered in the middle. It immediately rejects it using a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought if the person stayed unaware from the start of the act until the end. Once he remembers before the bread bakes, he is already exempt from a חטאת. So there is no need to take the bread out to save him from one.

keyTerms.meaning: He then remembered (in the middle of the act)
But we learned in a משנה (introduces a source used to challenge)
Those liable to bring a sin-offering
Their beginning was by mistake and their end was by mistake

steps.confusionAlert: The bread finishing its baking counts as the 'end' of the act. Remembering before it bakes means the end was not by mistake.

phrases.english: But rather, is it not where he then remembered?
Is he even liable?!
But we learned in a משנה:
All those liable for sin-offerings are not liable
unless their beginning was by mistake
and their end was by mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא לָאו דְּאִיהַדַּר וְאִידְּכַר, מִי מִחַיַּיב?! וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case of a person who never remembers was rejected, this tries the case of one who remembers in the middle.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the case where the person remembers before the bread bakes.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Once he remembers, he is already exempt from a חטאת, so there is nothing to save him from.

steps.title: The case where he acted on purpose also fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a case where the person put the bread in on purpose. It rejects this too, because then the question should have mentioned stoning, not a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he did it on purpose. But then the question should have said: 'before he comes to a prohibition punishable by stoning'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third case: the person acted on purpose and now regrets it. It rejects this based on the wording of רב ביבי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who breaks שבת on purpose is liable for סקילה, not a חטאת. A חטאת is only for mistakes. Since רב ביבי's question mentions a חטאת, it cannot be about a person who acted on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose, knowingly
A prohibition punishable by stoning
He should have said

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where he acted on purpose.
'Before he comes to a prohibition of stoning'
is what he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמֵזִיד. קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּבֹא לִידֵי אִיסּוּר סְקִילָה מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the mistake cases are rejected, the גמרא tries the opposite case of acting on purpose.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the question as being about someone who acted on purpose.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording mentions a חטאת, but acting on purpose brings סקילה.

steps.title: רב שילא: he acted by mistake, and the question is about other people
steps.stepSummary: רב שילא says the person did act by mistake. The question is whether the חכמים allowed other people to take the bread out for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שילא said: Really, the case is where he acted by mistake. And whom did they allow to take it out? Other people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שילא answers the problem from Step 7. Yes, the person who acted by mistake cannot be given permission, since he does not know anything is wrong. But other people who see what happened can be given permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the case as a mistake, which fits the word חטאת in the question. It also solves the problem of 'who is being given permission' by moving the permission to bystanders who know the bread is in the oven.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (we go back to the earlier case)
By mistake, unknowingly
To others

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the question from one about the sinner himself into a question about whether one person may act to save another from sin.

phrases.english: Rav Sheila said:
Actually, it is where he acted by mistake,
and to whom did they permit? To others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: All three cases failed, so רב שילא goes back to the first case (mistake) and fixes its problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines who is being given permission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the permission was for the person who put the bread in, which made no sense if he never remembered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission is for others, who can take the bread out to save the unaware person from a חטאת.

steps.title: רב ששת: we don't tell someone to sin so another can benefit
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects that we never tell a person to do something forbidden so that his friend will gain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: Do we tell a person, 'Sin so that your friend will benefit'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רב שילא's answer. Taking the bread out is itself forbidden (at least מדרבנן), so how could the חכמים let a bystander do it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב שילא's answer, the bystander does a forbidden act to save someone else from a bigger sin. רב ששת says that this is not how the rules work. A person is not told to sin, even a small sin, to help another person.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objected to it
Sin so that your friend will benefit

steps.whatToRemember: The search for רב ביבי's case has gone through mistake, remembering, and on purpose. Now רב שילא's 'others' answer faces רב ששת's principle: we don't tell a person to sin to help his friend.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet strongly objected to it:
And do we say to a person:
'Sin so that your friend will benefit'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וְכִי אוֹמְרִים לוֹ לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly attacks רב שילא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שילא's claim that others were allowed to take the bread out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking the bread out is forbidden. A person is not told to sin, even a small sin, in order to help someone else.

steps.title: רב אשי: The case is on purpose, and the wording is about stoning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי goes back to the case of putting the bread in on purpose. He fixes the wording so the question is about avoiding an איסור סקילה, not a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Really, the case is one where he did it on purpose. And change the wording to say: 'before he comes to an איסור סקילה (a sin punished by stoning).'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer. He says the person put the bread in on purpose, and the question should be read as 'before he comes to an איסור סקילה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא rejected the 'on purpose' case only because the question mentioned a חטאת, not stoning. רב אשי simply fixes the wording to say stoning. Now רב ששת's objection (step 11) no longer applies: the person himself removes the bread to save himself from a much bigger sin. He is not sinning so that someone else can gain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier answers)
Really / actually (going back to an idea that was set aside)
On purpose, knowing it is forbidden
And say instead (fixing the wording)
A sin punished by stoning, like baking on שבת on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is ignoring step 9. He agrees with it: the word חטאת does not fit an on-purpose case. That is exactly why he changes the wording to סקילה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Really, it is a case of doing it on purpose.
phrases.notes: Goes back to the case rejected in step 9.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא: קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּבֹא לִידֵי אִיסּוּר סְקִילָה.
phrases.english: And say: before he comes to a prohibition punished by stoning.
phrases.notes: Replaces 'before he becomes liable to a חטאת.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְעוֹלָם בְּמֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת rejects רב שילא's answer, רב אשי offers a new case: on purpose, with corrected wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a mistaken baker, or about letting others remove the bread for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The person acted on purpose and may remove the bread himself, to avoid the stoning-level sin of baking.

steps.title: רב אחא teaches it as a plain ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא does not teach רב ביבי's statement as a question. He teaches it as a clear ruling: you may remove the bread before you come to an איסור סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, taught it openly as a ruling: רב ביבי בר אביי said: If someone stuck bread in an oven, the חכמים allowed him to take it out before he comes to an איסור סקילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of רב ביבי's statement. In this version, it is not a question at all. It is a clear היתר to take the bread out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version supports רב אשי's reading: the issue is avoiding stoning, not a חטאת. It also settles the matter. Removing bread from the oven is only forbidden מדרבנן, so the חכמים allowed it to save a person from a stoning-level sin.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it openly, as a clear statement
Stuck (bread dough onto the wall of an oven)
Bread
To take it out (remove bread from the oven)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: if someone put bread in the oven on שבת, he may take it out before it bakes. That way he avoids the איסור סקילה of baking.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key principle: the חכמים may allow a small rabbinic איסור so that a person does not reach a much bigger, Torah-level sin.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava,
would teach it explicitly (as a ruling).
Rav Bivi bar Abaye said:
If one stuck bread in an oven,
they permitted him to remove it
before he comes to a prohibition punished by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the text that matches רב אשי's reading, now as a ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who stuck bread in an oven on שבת may remove it before it bakes, to avoid an איסור סקילה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Removing the bread is allowed in order to prevent the Torah-level sin of baking.

steps.title: Why is the poor person liable if a hand is not a 4x4 surface?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It asks: how can the poor person be liable when his hand is not a 4x4 טפחים place for עקירה and הנחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The poor person stretched out his hand (and he is liable). Why is he liable? Don't we need the lifting and the placing to be from on top of a place that is four טפחים by four טפחים? And that is missing here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the case in the משנה where the poor person reaches his hand in or out. It challenges the ruling that he is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be liable for carrying on שבת, one must lift (עקירה) and put down (הנחה) the object. These are normally done on a place at least 4x4 טפחים. A hand is much smaller, so it seems no real עקירה or הנחה happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Lifting an object from its place (the start of carrying)
Putting an object down (the end of carrying)
Four by four טפחים, the normal minimum size of a 'place'

phrases.english: 'The poor person extended his hand':
Why is he liable?
But don't we require lifting and placing

phrases.aramaic: מֵעַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.english: from on top of a place four by four (handbreadths),
and that is not present?

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ: אַמַּאי חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bread discussion and goes back to the משנה's case of the poor person's hand.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the poor person is חייב when the object is moved by his hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עקירה and הנחה need a 4x4 place; a hand is not 4x4, so there should be no liability.

steps.title: רבה: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that a 4x4 place is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי עקיבא, who said that we do not need a place of four by four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. He says the משנה matches the view of רבי עקיבא, who does not require a 4x4 place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that everyone requires a 4x4 place. רבה says not everyone does. According to רבי עקיבא even a small area like a hand is enough, so the poor person is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? (identifying the author of a משנה)
We do not require

phrases.english: Rabbah said: Whose (opinion) is this?
It is Rabbi Akiva, who said we do not require
a place of four by four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: הָא מַנִּי? — רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by naming the author of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא (הא מני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone requires a 4x4 place for עקירה and הנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא does not require a 4x4 place, and the משנה follows him.

steps.title: Proof from throwing across the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings a משנה: if someone throws from one private area to another, with a public area in between, רבי עקיבא says he is liable and the חכמים say he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone throws an object from a private domain to another private domain, and there is a public domain in the middle, רבי עקיבא says he is liable, and the חכמים say he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a source to show that רבי עקיבא really holds this way. This step sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The object only flies through the air over the רשות הרבים. It never lands on any surface, let alone a 4x4 one. Yet רבי עקיבא still holds him liable, which shows he does not require a 4x4 place.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה)
One who throws
Private domain
Public domain
They exempt (say he is not liable)

phrases.english: As we learned: One who throws from a private domain
to a private domain, with the public domain in the middle,
Rabbi Akiva holds him liable,
and the Sages exempt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַזּוֹרֵק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבה's claim about רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא does not require a 4x4 place for הנחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about throwing between two private domains across a public domain

steps.title: The reason: an object in the air counts as resting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the argument. רבי עקיבא holds that an object flying in the air counts as if it was put down. The חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds that we say: an object caught in the air is like one that was put down. And the חכמים hold that we do not say: an object caught in the air is like one that was put down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the argument, and this finishes רבה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the moment the object is in the air over the רשות הרבים, it counts as placed there, even with no surface at all. If no surface is needed, then surely a small hand is enough. So the poor person is liable according to רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (his view is)
Caught in the air (an object in mid-air)
Is like something that was put down

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא, so no 4x4 place is needed. That is why the משנה can make the poor person liable even though the object moved with his small hand.
steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים exempt the thrower because the object never landed in the רשות הרבים. This does not mean they hold that carrying across is allowed. They simply hold that, here, there was no הנחה in the public domain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds that we say:
'An object caught in the air is like one that was put down.'
And the Rabbis hold that we do not say:
'An object caught in the air is like one that was put down.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר אָמְרִינַן קְלוּטָה כְּמִי שֶׁהוּנְּחָה דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the משנה just quoted, which completes the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי עקיבא, an object in mid-air counts as placed. So a 4x4 surface is not needed, and the poor person's hand is enough for liability.

steps.title: Is רבה really sure that a flying object counts as put down?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבה's answer: does this mean רבה thinks it is obvious that קלוטה כמי שהונחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that it is obvious to רבה that an object caught in the air is treated as if it was put down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רבה. It points out that his answer seems to treat קלוטה כמי שהונחה as obvious, and the next line will question whether he really held that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer only works if קלוטה כמי שהונחה is a simple, settled rule for him. The word למימרא ('is this to say') signals that the גמרא is surprised by this. Usually this means the גמרא is about to show that רבה himself had a doubt about it somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is this to say...?' - an expression of surprise that opens a challenge
It is obvious to him; he has no doubt about it
An object 'caught' in the air, meaning it is flying through the airspace
Is considered as if it was put down (resting)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a ruling, and it is not the full question. It only opens the challenge. The real problem (that רבה himself asked about this) comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Is this to say that it is obvious to Rabba
phrases.notes: למימרא introduces surprise. The גמרא is questioning an assumption hidden in רבה's answer.

phrases.english: that an object caught in the air is considered as if it was put down?
phrases.notes: This is the rule behind רבה's answer. It is stated outright in step 17 as the reason for רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבה's answer (steps 15-17) and asks what it assumes: that קלוטה כמי שהונחה is obvious to him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's answer that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, based on קלוטה כמי שהונחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבה's answer depends on this rule being obvious, it is a problem if רבה elsewhere shows he was unsure about it. This line sets up that contradiction.
